title: ADW ecosystem hook integration
goal: Integrate all 51 validated ADW-scoped ecosystem hook ideas into agent-discipline-watcher: 38 built across ten epics, 13 explicitly deferred with reasons. ADW stays a deterministic, blocking-or-injecting discipline layer across its four clients (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi).
strategy: TDD per task on the existing 86-test pytest net, staged Lean rollout for every new blocking gate (observe-first per D7, promoted on adjudicated ledger evidence), with DevOps and responsible-engineering gates borrowed where a hook touches install, user prompts, or secrets.
strategy_rationale: Hook code is logic-heavy and bug-prone, so the delivery strategy is test-first. The real product risk is not code correctness but gate behavior in live sessions: a false-blocking Stop hook is worse than no hook. So the riskiest assumption is tested by the smallest slice (dispatcher plus Stop gate, live-verified) before the wide build-out, and every new gate ships in observe until the adjudicated ledger shows its precision.

decisions.choice: Keep one canonical Python engine (hooks/lib) behind thin per-client adapters. No HTTP service, no MCP server, no daemon. The type:http and mcp_tool hook types are deferred.
decisions.tradeoff: Per-client adapters must be extended by hand for each new event, but ADW gains no network dependency, no auth surface, and no daemon lifecycle to babysit.

decisions.choice: All event-schema knowledge lives in one payload-normalization module (hooks/lib/payloads.py) with contract tests per documented field. Hooks never read raw payload keys directly.
decisions.tradeoff: One extra indirection per hook, but schema drift across Claude Code versions breaks one tested file instead of eleven hooks.

decisions.choice: Every hook lands with a test in the hooks/test_*.py pattern plus the full pytest gate. Wiring tasks additionally re-run merge-config tests. A small live end-to-end verification (E10-T1) proves acceptance behavior without replacing focused tests.
decisions.tradeoff: More test code to maintain than ad-hoc hook scripts, in exchange for regression evidence on every change.

decisions.choice: Session-scoped state (freeze lease, first-touch acks, failure streaks, dead ends, compaction snapshot) is durable JSON on disk under ~/.agent-discipline/state/<session_id>/, written atomically, cleaned by SessionEnd.
decisions.tradeoff: State files need lifecycle management, but gates survive crash, compaction, and hook-process restarts, which in-memory state cannot.

decisions.choice: Work splits by hook event and capability (delivery slices), not by technical layer. Contended files (pre_write.py, stop.py, prompt_submit.py, the snippets) get explicit sequential dependency chains so no two open tasks own the same file.
decisions.tradeoff: Some cross-epic dependencies (the verify lib feeds E2), but zero merge collisions between parallel workers.

decisions.choice: Stdlib-only Python 3.11+, matching the existing codebase. Atomic file replacement and locking follow CPython primary-documented behavior (os.replace, fcntl).
decisions.tradeoff: No third-party ergonomics, in exchange for a zero-dependency install on all clients.

decisions.choice: Every gate has three states in central config: off, observe, and enforce. New gates ship in observe, where the full check runs and the ledger records a would_block row but nothing blocks. The metric is fully producible: every entry script runs through the shared main wrapper, which emits one observed heartbeat row per invocation and stamps every ledger row with the session's current turn_id from session state, stop.py advances that turn counter on the first Stop of a turn only, never on a stop_hook_active retry after a block (the pseudo-Stop equivalent advances it on clients without Stop per the parity matrix, and a family with no turn producer on its client is reported per-invocation and labeled as such), so the denominator is the count of distinct observed turn_ids, never raw invocations, which a multi-fire hook would inflate. lib/config logs a state-transition row whenever a family's effective state changes (the producer for the override signal), and the observe report renders each family's would_block sample for the weekly review, persists the lead's true-or-false-signal labels as adjudication rows in the ledger (the adjudication that would_block incidence alone cannot supply), and computes the per-family adjudicated false-signal rate per 20 observed turns, the number E10-T2 consumes. Promotion to enforce requires a burn-in window of at least one week and an adjudicated false-signal rate at or under 1 per 20 observed turns for that family, decided at E10-T2. The existing three families keep their current enforce defaults. No exceptions among shipped gates: the TaskCompleted scan, the taint self-protection rule, and the commit-message scan also start in observe. Explicit opt-in features (freeze lease, first-touch gate, at-mention rule, the injection maps, the data_boundary tier) are user-invoked, not silently shipped, so they enforce on enable, and their default-off wording refers to the feature switch, not a gate state.
decisions.tradeoff: Slower protection rollout and a weekly adjudication chore for the lead, but the false-block metric has a defined producer for every term before enforcement, and rollback is a config flip.

decisions.choice: Defer all non-deterministic hook types (type:prompt, type:agent, the LLM-judge Stop gate, prompt/agent SubagentStop QA): they break ADW's deterministic-blocking contract, and agent hooks are documented as experimental.
decisions.tradeoff: Judgment-call rules (hollow test versus trivial test) stay regex-approximate, but every block stays reproducible and explainable.

decisions.choice: The UserPromptSubmit firewall defaults to injecting a warning, not blocking, on matched human prompts. Block-mode is an explicit config opt-in.
decisions.tradeoff: A user can still push past the warning, but ADW never silently erases a human's prompt by default, which is the higher harm.

decisions.choice: Blocking parity is capability-bounded per adapter, never assumed. Pi's adapter has no pre-execution hook point, so blocking gates degrade to post-hoc findings on Pi. OpenCode's pseudo-Stop is injection-only. A gate task for a both-scoped idea is complete only when the parity matrix row records per-client status (wired, degraded, or not available), and touching only Claude wiring never marks such an idea done.
decisions.tradeoff: Honest degraded parity is documented instead of pretended uniform enforcement, at the cost of a per-gate matrix row to maintain.

decisions.choice: One entry script per event-and-matcher pair, never two hooks racing on the same surface. Where several capabilities share a surface they compose inside the entry script in a fixed order: input rewrites first, then structural gates, then content scans, first deny wins, injected contexts concatenate. Concretely: pre_write.py orchestrates the edit-PreToolUse pipeline (redaction rewrite, protected, freeze, first-touch, taint, scan), record.py orchestrates PostToolUse (edit journal, scan, verify recipes, spill, output redaction), and pre_commit.py and pre_mcp.py own their disjoint matchers. Redaction and the formatter therefore land as lib modules called from these orchestrators, not as separate hooks.
decisions.tradeoff: The orchestrator files grow and their ownership chains get longer, but handler order and merge semantics are code, not an unspecified property of client hook dispatch.

decisions.choice: Command-bearing config is honored only after a user-owned trust grant recorded outside the repo (~/.agent-discipline/trust/<repo-fingerprint>), written by the installed CLI: 'agent-discipline trust' run in the repo, which works from any cwd because install.sh already links bin/agent-discipline into ~/.local/bin. Without the grant, verify, formatter, lint, typecheck, test, coverage, and AST recipes no-op with a visible note. Commands execute as argv lists, never through a shell. An end-to-end test proves the grant flow (trust, revoke, moved repo) from a temporary target repo after a sandbox install.
decisions.tradeoff: One extra explicit step per repo before quality gates run, in exchange for a checked-in .agent-discipline.json in an untrusted repo never executing code automatically.

decisions.choice: record.py's per-call scan is canonical and never suppressed. PostToolBatch is additive only: it reads the ledger rows already written for the batch and reports only new cross-file findings, so nothing is buffered and nothing is lost if PostToolBatch never fires. Correlation uses the per-call tool_use_id, carried in the payload contract and stored in every PostToolUse ledger row, matched against the ids in the PostToolBatch tool_calls array. If the live payloads lack the id (the contract test and the E10 smoke check for it), batch.py drops ledger dedupe entirely and restricts itself to intrinsically cross-file rules, its documented degraded mode.
decisions.tradeoff: A batch can surface two block messages (per-call plus cross-file) instead of one perfectly merged report, but no finding ever depends on an event that might not exist or a correlation field that might not arrive.

decisions.choice: Fail-safe registration: an unknown event key in a client config is treated as able to break config parsing before any handler runs, never assumed to be a dormant no-op. Therefore events register train by train behind the E10-T0 gate, every wiring task proves the merged config in a sandbox HOME (parse-back plus the client's own config validation where one exists) before the lead installs live, the parity matrix records the minimum client version per event, and the timestamped install backups are the immediate rollback when a client still rejects a key.
decisions.tradeoff: Wiring lands in more, smaller steps than one bulk registration, but a client that chokes on a new event key is caught in a throwaway HOME, not in the operator's live config.

epics.title: Foundation: dispatcher, state, payload contracts, ledger
epics.outcome: Every later hook plugs into a data-driven dispatcher, a tested payload layer, durable session state, and a findings ledger. Nothing user-visible changes yet except if-field scoping and async flags on existing wiring.

stories.title: Core libraries: dispatch, payloads, and gate config
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want one dispatch table, one payload contract, one state store, and one ledger, so that eleven new hooks share tested plumbing instead of reinventing it.
acceptance: run.sh routes events from a single data-driven table, one entry script per event-and-matcher pair (D11), and unknown events still exit 2 with usage

lib/payloads.py exposes typed accessors for every documented field the plan consumes (session_id, cwd, tool_name, last_assistant_message, stop_hook_active, agent_id, agent_type, agent_transcript_path, prompt, source, file_path, error, is_interrupt, duration_ms, tool_calls, task_id, task_subject), each with a contract test
lib/config.py carries the central gate-state schema: every gate family resolves to off, observe, or enforce, with observe running the full check and writing would_block rows without blocking (D7)

every new hook module follows the existing pattern: an importable module exposing run(payload, config) with I/O only via the hookio helpers, so test files import it directly and call run() the way test_hooks.py already does

tasks.t: E1-S1-T1: Data-driven run.sh dispatcher
tasks.risk: POSIX sh portability across macOS and Linux, covered by a test invoking run.sh directly.

tasks.t: E1-S1-T3: Payload contract module (lib/payloads.py)
tasks.risk: Carries the plan's residual event-schema risk by design (risks[0]). That is its job.

tasks.t: E1-S1-T5: Central gate-state config schema (lib/config.py)
tasks.risk: Schema creep. The task defines only the keys tasks in this plan consume, nothing speculative.

stories.title: Core libraries: durable session state and findings ledger
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want one dispatch table, one payload contract, one state store, and one ledger, so that eleven new hooks share tested plumbing instead of reinventing it.
acceptance: lib/session_state.py survives process restart and concurrent writers (atomic replace), keyed by session_id, and offers a sweep API that removes stale session dirs, the janitor for a missed SessionEnd

every gate decision appends one JSONL ledger row with hook, rule, duration_ms, tool_use_id where present, and an outcome from the enum block, inject, would_block, no_edits, and record.py journals every successful edit (path, tool, ts) so completion gates know what changed this session
every entry script runs through the shared main wrapper, which emits one observed heartbeat row per invocation, the denominator for the D7 metric and the producer for the E10-T1 heartbeat check

tasks.t: E1-S1-T2: Durable session state store (lib/session_state.py)
tasks.risk: Concurrent hook invocations racing on one file, mitigated by atomic replace plus an fcntl lock in the read-modify-write helper.

tasks.t: E1-S1-T4: Findings ledger, session edit journal, heartbeat wrapper, observe report
tasks.risk: Ledger writes must never block or fail a hook. Append errors are swallowed with a stderr note. Heartbeat rows are one line each so volume stays trivial.

stories.title: Existing-wiring hardening and parity map
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want the existing wiring scoped tighter and a per-client event availability matrix, so that new-event wiring tasks have a factual basis per client.
acceptance: the Claude snippet's Bash pre-commit hook carries the documented if filter for git commit while pre_commit.py's own parser stays as the cross-client backstop
an async-flag policy exists: log-only hooks declare async true in the Claude snippet

a parity matrix (README section) states, per client and per event used in this plan, wired or degraded or not-available, from each client's primary docs, including the Pi post-hoc-only and OpenCode injection-only-Stop limits
HOOK_LIFECYCLES in merge-codex-config.py lists every event ADW wires, with a merge test asserting the list matches the snippet

tasks.t: E1-S2-T1: if-field scoping plus async flag policy on the Claude snippet
tasks.risk: The if syntax must match the documented permission-rule grammar exactly. The merge-config test asserts the literal.

tasks.t: E1-S2-T2: Cross-client event parity matrix plus merge-script generalization
tasks.risk: Codex and Pi docs may be thin. Where undocumented, the matrix says unknown and the gate ships Claude-only. A missed HOOK_LIFECYCLES entry silently corrupts reinstall merges, so the merge tests assert one entry per wired event.

epics.title: Turn-end and completion enforcement (Stop family)
epics.outcome: ADW can refuse to end a turn, a subagent, a task, or a tool batch while discipline findings or failed verification stand. This is the MVP value epic.

stories.title: Stop gate
stories.why: As an operator, I want the turn blocked when the final message claims done without evidence or violates prose discipline, so that unproved claims never end a turn silently.
acceptance: stop.py scans last_assistant_message with the existing scanner families plus an unproved-done rule in lib/done_claims.py (done, fixed, complete, or passing language with no verification evidence in the message), keeping scanner.py untouched
stop_hook_active is honored with no re-block loops, and the documented cap of eight consecutive blocks is respected by design
the optional verify mode runs trusted repo-declared commands, ships in observe per D7, and blocks on failure only once the family is promoted to enforce
every decision lands in the ledger

tasks.t: E2-S1-T1: stop.py discipline plus unproved-done gate
tasks.risk: Scanning final prose can over-fire on quoted user text. The rule set starts narrow with the done-claim patterns the clean-coder family already defines.

tasks.t: E2-S1-T2: Verify-command Stop gate (deterministic test gate)
tasks.risk: Long test suites at Stop time add latency. The verify config carries a per-command timeout and the gate reports elapsed time to the ledger.

stories.title: SubagentStop coverage
stories.why: As an operator, I want delegated work held to the same turn-end discipline, so that a subagent cannot hand back unproved claims invisibly.
acceptance: subagent_stop.py scans the subagent's last_assistant_message with the same rules as stop.py
agent_type matcher support is documented, and ledger rows carry agent_id and agent_type

tasks.t: E2-S2-T1: subagent_stop.py scan
tasks.risk: Transcript-file scanning stays out of this task (message-only) until the ledger shows need. Transcript files can be huge.

stories.title: TaskCompleted gate
stories.why: As an operator, I want a task blocked from completing while its changed files carry findings or its verify matrix fails, so that a bad done lands per task, not at turn end.
acceptance: task_completed.py uses the corrected fields (task_id, task_subject, optional teammate and team) and the corrected control (exit 2 or continue false), not the disproven task_result or decision-block fields
scans files recorded as changed this session (ledger) and, when configured, runs the verify matrix scoped by changed-file categories
documented as Claude-only until the parity matrix says otherwise

tasks.t: E2-S3-T1: task_completed.py verification gate
tasks.risk: The event is tied to the agent-team task system and the idea confidence is medium. Observe mode accrues evidence before anything blocks.

stories.title: PostToolBatch single-pass scan
stories.why: As an operator, I want one coherent block message per parallel edit batch, so that findings across simultaneous writes are deduplicated and cross-file patterns are visible.
acceptance: record.py's per-call scan stays canonical and is never suppressed or buffered (D13)

batch.py correlates via tool_use_id (payload contract and ledger row field) between the tool_calls array and the batch's PostToolUse rows, and reports only new cross-file findings, so its dedupe is of its own output and nothing is lost if PostToolBatch never fires
when live payloads lack tool_use_id, batch.py drops ledger dedupe and restricts itself to intrinsically cross-file rules, the degraded mode D13 documents

tasks.t: E2-S4-T1: batch.py additive cross-file pass (D13)
tasks.risk: Correlation rests on tool_use_id arriving in both payloads. The degraded mode and the batch-absent case are both explicit tests, so neither assumption can fail silently.

stories.title: Failure-event handling
stories.why: As an operator, I want repeated tool failures met with deterministic guidance and unhealthy MCP servers short-circuited, so that the agent neither weakens changes to dodge errors nor burns turns on dead providers.
acceptance: failure.py records per-tool and per-target failure streaks (error, is_interrupt, duration_ms) in session state
a streak threshold injects a fix-the-root-cause instruction naming the repeated failure
MCP substate: a server is marked unhealthy on failure with 30s base exponential backoff capped at 10min, and a PreToolUse consult blocks calls to known-unhealthy servers until backoff expiry

tasks.t: E2-S5-T1: failure.py plus MCP circuit breaker
tasks.risk: Backoff state is keyed per session first. Cross-session escalation only if the ledger shows need. Fail-safe: if PostToolUseFailure never fires, the health substate stays empty and pre_mcp allows everything, degraded but harmless.

stories.title: E2 wiring and parity
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want the E2 events registered on every client that supports them, so the gates actually fire on all four clients or the gap is a documented fact.
acceptance: E2-W-T0 wires the Stop event alone and heads the shared-file chain, so E10-T0 can smoke the riskiest bet before anything else goes live
the Claude snippet then gains SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, PostToolBatch, PostToolUseFailure, and the mcp__* PreToolUse consult entries, with run.sh routing each event, only after E10-T0 passes
the Codex TOML gains the events the parity matrix confirms, and HOOK_LIFECYCLES covers each of them (E1-S2-T2 groundwork)
the OpenCode and Pi adapters are extended in their own tasks below for every plan event their APIs support, and every gate's parity row records wired, degraded, or not-available per client (D10)
install.sh and merge scripts stay idempotent on re-run, proven by a sandbox install into a temporary HOME with every merged client config parsed back cleanly

tasks.t: E2-W-T0: Wire Stop only (the MVP slice)
tasks.risk: Smallest possible live surface by design. If Stop misbehaves here, only one hook needs unwinding.

tasks.t: E2-W-T1: Wire the remaining E2 events on Claude and Codex (post-smoke)
tasks.risk: Codex event availability may be narrower than Claude's. The parity matrix decides, with gaps documented in SKILL.md at E10-T3.

tasks.t: E2-W-T2: Extend the OpenCode adapter (all plan events its API supports)
tasks.risk: OpenCode's plugin API may expose none of the new lifecycle points, in which case this task's deliverable is the documented gap plus the strongest post-hoc approximation, not silence. If the installed node predates type stripping, the task substitutes the repo's available TS runner and records it in README.

tasks.t: E2-W-T3: Extend the Pi adapter (post-hoc surfaces only, with its own tests)
tasks.risk: The temptation is to fake a block by erroring post-hoc. The task documents degraded mode honestly instead, and revisits only when Pi grows a pre-execution hook point. If the installed node predates type stripping, the task substitutes the repo's available TS runner and records it in README.

epics.title: Prompt and context boundary (UserPromptSubmit plus JIT injection)
epics.outcome: Discipline applies at the source: human prompts that induce violations get a deterministic warning (or opt-in block), and targeted convention context is injected exactly when relevant.

stories.title: Prompt firewall
stories.why: As an operator, I want prompts like 'just comment it out' or 'skip the tests' met with an injected discipline reminder before the agent complies, so violations stop at the source.
acceptance: prompt_submit.py matches a small reviewed rule list against the prompt field, injects additionalContext by default (D9), and offers block-mode as a config opt-in
the at-mention rule (config-gated, default off) blocks literal @filename tokens forcing an explicit Read, for data-boundary mode
the keyword-to-context map (config-gated, default off) injects mapped guidance deterministically
no prompt text is persisted anywhere

tasks.t: E3-S1-T1: prompt_submit.py firewall (inject-first)
tasks.risk: Blocking human input is the highest-harm failure in the plan. D9 keeps the default inject-only. The 30s default timeout on this event is noted in tests.

tasks.t: E3-S1-T2: At-mention bypass rule (config-gated)
tasks.risk: Aggressive when on, since it blocks a convenience feature. Hence default off and tied to the E7 data-boundary mode.

tasks.t: E3-S1-T3: Keyword-to-context injection map (config-gated)
tasks.risk: Context bloat if maps grow. The injected snippet size is capped and reported to the ledger.

stories.title: Just-in-time convention injection on edits
stories.why: As an operator, I want path-scoped conventions injected at the moment of the edit, so guidance arrives before the model commits to an approach instead of only rejecting after.
acceptance: pre_write.py consults a path-glob-to-snippet map (config) and returns the snippet as context alongside allow
injection happens at most once per file per session (session state)

tasks.t: E3-S2-T1: Path-scoped JIT convention injection in pre_write
tasks.risk: pre_write.py is the plan's contention hotspot. This chain is strictly sequential (D5).

stories.title: E3 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want UserPromptSubmit registered where available.
acceptance: Claude snippet plus run.sh route added, other clients per the parity matrix, merge tests updated

tasks.t: E3-W-T1: Wire UserPromptSubmit (Claude and Codex)
tasks.risk: None beyond shared-file sequencing.

epics.title: Self-protection and scope discipline
epics.outcome: ADW defends its own leash (config tamper seal, ConfigChange defense) and offers structural scope enforcement (freeze lease, first-touch gate, taint sequences).

stories.title: Quality-config tamper seal
stories.why: As an operator, I want edits to linter, formatter, typecheck, hook, and ignore configs and to ADW's own wiring blocked unless explicitly authorized, so the agent cannot green-light checks by weakening the checker.
acceptance: a protected-path policy in lib/protected.py blocks edits to existing protected files, allows first-time creation, and fails closed on stat errors (EACCES and EPERM treated as exists)
case-insensitive basename matching for case-insensitive filesystems
explicit authorization via config or a documented env var, with authorized changes invalidating cached verify results and landing in the ledger
new blanket suppressions in source edits (file-level lint disables, blanket type-ignores) are blocked unless policy permits them

tasks.t: E4-S1-T1: Tamper seal in pre_write (merges the ECC config lock and the tamper seal)
tasks.risk: An over-broad protected set annoys legitimate config work. The authorization path must be one obvious step.

stories.title: ConfigChange self-tampering defense
stories.why: As an operator, I want mid-session changes to ADW's hook registration blocked, so a prompt-injected instruction cannot silently disable enforcement.
acceptance: config_change.py blocks changes whose source is user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, or skills when the changed file matches ADW wiring or skill files
policy_settings changes are logged only, since the docs say blocking is ignored there

tasks.t: E4-S2-T1: config_change.py hook
tasks.risk: Must not block the user's own deliberate reconfiguration flow. Scope strictly to ADW-owned paths.

stories.title: Session-scoped edit freeze lease
stories.why: As an operator, I want an opt-in freeze command that denies edits outside a directory boundary until I widen it, so scope creep is structurally impossible during focused work.
acceptance: CLI subcommands freeze, unfreeze, and status write the lease to session state
pre_write denies (permissionDecision deny) resolved paths outside the boundary with the lease named in the reason

tasks.t: E4-S3-T1: Freeze lease (CLI plus pre_write deny)
tasks.risk: Path resolution must match the client's (symlinks, relative paths). Reuse the record.py resolution approach and test both.

stories.title: First-touch fact-forcing gate (opt-in)
stories.why: As an operator, I want the first edit to each file per session to force an explicit impact statement, so change-impact thinking happens before the write, not after.
acceptance: default off. When on, the first Edit or Write per file per session is denied with an instruction to state importers and callers, affected APIs, and the current instruction. The denial marks the file acknowledged in session state so the retry passes
destructive Bash (rm -rf and configured patterns) gets the same one-pause gate requiring listed targets and a rollback plan

tasks.t: E4-S4-T1: First-touch gate in pre_write plus the Bash destructive gate
tasks.risk: Pure friction if left on globally. Default off, and the reason text tells the user how to disable it.

stories.title: Cross-call behavioral taint sequences
stories.why: As an operator, I want read-secret-then-network and download-then-execute sequences blocked, so multi-step exfiltration patterns are caught that single-payload scans cannot see.
acceptance: record.py (PostToolUse) appends tool events to a session event log, and lib/taint.py evaluates a small named-rule set (sensitive-read-then-network, write-then-build poisoning, sensitive-read-then-MCP) on PreToolUse for Bash, Write, and Edit
rules also block Bash commands manipulating ADW's own config or allowlist
each rule has a named id in block reasons and ledger rows

tasks.t: E4-S5-T1: lib/taint.py sequence rules plus the event log feed
tasks.risk: False positives on legitimate read-then-curl workflows. All taint rules ship in observe with a ledger-first burn-in (D7).

stories.title: E4 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want ConfigChange registered and the CLI reachable.
acceptance: ConfigChange snippet plus route. install.sh already links bin/agent-discipline. Merge tests updated

tasks.t: E4-W-T1: Wire ConfigChange (Claude only per matrix)
tasks.risk: None beyond shared-file sequencing.

epics.title: Compaction resilience
epics.outcome: Discipline state survives compaction: PreCompact snapshots session state, and the already-wired SessionStart(compact) path re-injects the full contract plus the snapshot.

stories.title: PreCompact snapshot with a scoped veto
stories.why: As an operator, I want session discipline state snapshotted before compaction, and compaction vetoed only while a blocking gate is unresolved, so enforcement context cannot be summarized away mid-gate.
acceptance: pre_compact.py writes the snapshot (active leases, ack sets, streaks, pending block state) to session state and handles the manual and auto matchers
the veto (block decision) fires only when a blocking gate is mid-flight, and the default is allow

tasks.t: E5-S1-T1: pre_compact.py snapshot and scoped veto
tasks.risk: An over-eager veto can trap a session at full context. The veto condition is narrow and logged.

stories.title: SessionStart(compact) contract re-injection
stories.why: As an operator, I want the full discipline contract re-injected after compaction, so long sessions do not lose the rules.
acceptance: session_start.py branches on source: compact gets the full contract plus a one-line snapshot summary, startup keeps today's line. Wiring already matches compact on Claude and Codex

tasks.t: E5-S2-T1: session_start.py compact-path enrichment plus janitor call
tasks.risk: The injected contract size must stay small. Cap and test the byte size.

stories.title: E5 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want PreCompact registered.
acceptance: PreCompact snippet plus route on clients per the parity matrix

tasks.t: E5-W-T1: Wire PreCompact
tasks.risk: None beyond shared-file sequencing.

epics.title: Repo verification tier (config-driven quality gates, trust-gated, observe-first)
epics.outcome: One verify runner plus per-category recipes (format, lint delta, typecheck, impacted tests, coverage, AST rules, commit messages) give runtime evidence that text scanning cannot. Entirely config-driven, inert without the D12 trust grant, and observe-first per D7.

stories.title: Verify runner core
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want one runner for repo-declared checks with changed-file category mapping, so six quality gates share one execution and reporting path.
acceptance: lib/verify.py: a declared matrix in .agent-discipline.json (category to commands), changed-file-to-category mapping, fail-fast, per-command timeout, compact structured failures, ledger rows with elapsed time

trust boundary (D12): command-bearing config is inert until a user-owned grant exists at ~/.agent-discipline/trust/<repo-fingerprint>, written by the installed CLI 'agent-discipline trust' run in the repo. Without it every recipe no-ops with a visible note. Commands execute as argv lists, never through a shell
an end-to-end test proves the documented command works from a temporary target repo after a sandbox install: trust, revoke, and moved-repo, so the boundary is usable, not just fail-closed

tasks.t: E6-S1-T1: lib/verify.py runner with the trust boundary
tasks.risk: A hook that runs automatically in an untrusted repo must never execute that repo's config. The trust grant is the whole defense, so its tests cover the no-grant, revoked-grant, and moved-repo cases end to end.

stories.title: Formatter fixed-point
stories.why: As an operator, I want touched files formatted to a fixed point after each edit with non-convergence blocking, so formatting noise never reaches review.
acceptance: a config map from language to formatter runs on the touched file only, check-mode verifies convergence, changed bytes return the path as context to force a reread, and crashes or non-convergence block
opt-in: this is ADW's only mutating hook and the config key says so explicitly

tasks.t: E6-S2-T1: lib/format_fix.py post-edit formatter recipe
tasks.risk: Breaks ADW's non-mutating norm. Isolated in its own lib module, opt-in, never bundled with scan config.

stories.title: Baseline-aware lint delta gate
stories.why: As an operator, I want only newly introduced lint diagnostics blocked, so legacy debt stays visible without freezing work.
acceptance: the baseline is captured lazily once per session on the first post-edit check (keyed by session_id in session state, which keeps all work inside lib and avoids owning session_start.py), post-edit lint runs on the touched file or package and blocks only new diagnostics in structured file, line, and rule form, and the baseline recomputes on base-revision or lint-config change

tasks.t: E6-S3-T1: lib/lint_delta.py plus lazy baseline capture
tasks.risk: Baseline staleness produces wrong deltas. Recompute triggers are tested explicitly.

stories.title: Content-hashed typecheck gate
stories.why: As an operator, I want fresh type errors blocked cheaply after typed-language edits, so cross-file type breakage is caught before review.
acceptance: locate the owning package, run the no-output typecheck, cache keyed by config-file hashes (the verified prior art) with a full-input hash as stretch, block on fresh errors, and offer an uncached full check at completion

tasks.t: E6-S4-T1: lib/typecheck.py cached gate
tasks.risk: Cache invalidation bugs cause stale passes. The cache starts conservative (config-hash only) so misses cost time, not correctness.

stories.title: Impact-selected tests on edits
stories.why: As an operator, I want the affected tests run immediately after a source edit, so behavioral evidence arrives per edit, not per turn.
acceptance: adapters for jest --findRelatedTests and pytest-testmon, failing assertions returned as blocking feedback, and the full suite reserved for Stop, TaskCompleted, or commit

tasks.t: E6-S5-T1: lib/impacted.py test selection adapters
tasks.risk: testmon and jest availability varies per repo. The adapter degrades to declared verify commands when selectors are absent.

stories.title: Differential coverage ratchet
stories.why: As an operator, I want changed-line coverage below policy blocked at completion or commit, so new debt is stopped while legacy coverage stays visible.
acceptance: diff-cover and coverage.py integration, changed-line and changed-branch thresholds, and rejection of a drop from the base-branch baseline

tasks.t: E6-S6-T1: lib/coverage_gate.py ratchet
tasks.risk: Needs diff-cover present in the target repo. The gate no-ops with a documented note when absent.

stories.title: AST-native forbidden-API and architecture rules
stories.why: As an operator, I want project-owned ast-grep or Semgrep rules run on changed files with rule ids and precise ranges, so code-pattern policy is structural, not regex-lexical.
acceptance: the adapter runs project rules on changed files at PostToolUse and diff-wide at commit or TaskCompleted, blocks with rule id plus range, and reserves regex for non-code files

tasks.t: E6-S7-T1: lib/ast_rules.py adapter
tasks.risk: ast-grep and semgrep are external binaries. The adapter detects availability and no-ops with a documented note when absent.

stories.title: Commit-message gate
stories.why: As an operator, I want commit messages extracted from -m payloads and scanned (discipline families plus an optional conventional-commit format) before Bash executes, so commit text meets the same bar as file text.
acceptance: pre_commit.py extracts every -m and message-file payload with its existing shell-aware parser, scans with the scanner families, applies the optional format policy from config, and lets editor-only forms pass unless strict mode is on

tasks.t: E6-S8-T1: Commit-message extraction and scan in pre_commit
tasks.risk: Message extraction across quoting styles. Reuse the existing tested shlex path.

stories.title: E6 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want the verification recipes reachable from record.py, stop.py, and task_completed.py per config.
acceptance: record.py consults configured recipes post-edit, stop and task_completed run the full tier, snippets are updated where a new registration is needed, and every recipe is inert without the trust grant and observe-first per D7

tasks.t: E6-W-T1: Integrate verify recipes into the hook flow
tasks.risk: Latency stacking when several recipes are on. The runner's ledger timing makes it visible and the config docs recommend a budget.

epics.title: Data boundary (secrets and redaction, opt-in)
epics.outcome: A deterministic secret-block tier plus an opt-in pseudonymization boundary with a persistent, lock-guarded mapping, and spilled-output scanning so indirection is part of the payload. No separate hook registrations: per D11 the rewrites ride the pre_write and record.py orchestrators, so E7 needs no wiring task of its own.

stories.title: Secret block tier
stories.why: As an operator, I want true secrets (key, token, and credential patterns) blocked at write, commit, and prompt, so secrets never pass a boundary in plain form.
acceptance: a new secrets scanner family, config-gated, with a reviewed pattern set and per-rule ids, available to every scan_all caller: pre_write and pre_commit pick it up with no file edits, and the prompt boundary consumes it through E3-S1-T1's scanner integration
blocked values never reach the ledger or reports in plain form (fingerprint only)

tasks.t: E7-S1-T1: Secrets family in the scanner
tasks.risk: Pattern false positives on high-entropy non-secrets. Start with well-known prefixed formats.

stories.title: Pseudonymization boundary (Claude-only decision fields)
stories.why: As an operator, I want lower-risk identifiers consistently pseudonymized via updatedInput and updatedToolOutput with one stable mapping, so scrubbed sessions stay coherent.
acceptance: lib/pseudonym.py holds the persistent mapping under an exclusive flock on a sidecar lockfile, with one synthetic replacement per matched value across concurrent invocations

the input rewrite (updatedInput) runs first inside pre_write's orchestration and the output rewrite (updatedToolOutput) inside record.py's (D11), so rewrite-then-scan order is code, not racing hook registrations. Both default off, enabled only by data_boundary config
documented Claude-only (the decision fields are unavailable elsewhere), with other clients getting the block tier only

tasks.t: E7-S2-T1: lib/pseudonym.py mapping store (keyed HMAC)
tasks.risk: The mapping store and the key are separately sensitive. The store holds pseudonym-to-HMAC only, and the key never enters the repo or the ledger.

tasks.t: E7-S2-T2: lib/redact_input.py wired first in pre_write (updatedInput)
tasks.risk: Rewriting tool input can corrupt edits if patterns overmatch. Scoped to configured identifier classes only.

tasks.t: E7-S2-T3: lib/redact_output.py wired last in record.py (updatedToolOutput)
tasks.risk: The same overmatch risk on outputs, with the same scoping.

stories.title: Spilled-output scanning
stories.why: As an operator, I want spill stubs (truncated, preview, and output-file indirection) scanned at their source up to 1 MiB, so hidden content is part of the payload.
acceptance: lib/spill.py recognizes the stub heuristics, reads the spilled path capped at 1 MiB, runs block rules against the hidden content, and is wired from record.py

tasks.t: E7-S3-T1: lib/spill.py plus record.py integration
tasks.risk: record.py contention with E6-W-T1, sequenced after it.

stories.title: Human policy gate
stories.why: As the owner, I decide the redaction policy (identifier classes, retention of the mapping store, custody and rotation of the HMAC key, who may enable data_boundary mode) before the tier can be switched on.
acceptance: a short written policy in the repo docs covering identifier classes, mapping retention, and HMAC key custody plus rotation, and data_boundary mode refuses to enable without it

tasks.t: E7-H-T1: Redaction policy decision
checks: grep -Eqi '^## .*redaction.*policy' README.md && grep -Eqi 'identifier classes' README.md && grep -Eqi 'mapping (store )?retention' README.md && grep -Eqi 'HMAC key custody' README.md && grep -Eqi 'rotation' README.md
tasks.risk: Without this gate the tier could ship with unexamined privacy defaults.

epics.title: Negative memory (dead-end registry)
epics.outcome: Failed approaches become deterministic warnings: mined at Stop and SubagentStop, injected at UserPromptSubmit, optionally blocking reintroduction at PreToolUse.

stories.title: Dead-end registry pipeline
stories.why: As an operator, I want tried-and-reverted approaches remembered outside the repo and surfaced when they are about to be retried, so sessions stop rediscovering the same dead ends.
acceptance: a repo-keyed JSONL store outside the repo with a schema of approach fingerprint, evidence pointer, created, and expiry
miners on Stop and SubagentStop detect tried-and-reverted hunks from the session ledger and transcript
UserPromptSubmit injects a DEAD END card on match, and the PreToolUse similarity check warns by default and blocks only when configured

tasks.t: E8-S1-T1: lib/deadends.py store plus similarity fingerprinting
tasks.risk: Similarity threshold tuning. Fixture-driven tests with real revert examples.

tasks.t: E8-S1-T2: Stop and SubagentStop dead-end miners
tasks.risk: Noisy mining mislabels legitimate iteration as dead ends (risks[7]). Entries carry evidence pointers and expire.

tasks.t: E8-S1-T3: UserPromptSubmit dead-end warning card
tasks.risk: Card size capped, one card per prompt.

tasks.t: E8-S1-T4: PreToolUse reintroduction guard (warn-first)
tasks.risk: After five integrations pre_write needs the simplification pass this task's craft gate mandates.

stories.title: E8 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want the registry flush wired into PreCompact and SessionEnd.
acceptance: pre_compact and session_end flush pending mining state, and no new events are needed

tasks.t: E8-W-T1: Registry lifecycle wiring
tasks.risk: None beyond shared-file sequencing.

epics.title: Telemetry and audit
epics.outcome: ADW measures itself: which prose rules deserve promotion (dead-rules scorecard), which gates fire (the ledger from E1), what loaded when (InstructionsLoaded), and clean shutdown (SessionEnd).

stories.title: Dead-rules compliance telemetry
stories.why: As the maintainer, I want CLAUDE.md parsed into atomic rules with per-rule relevance and violation tallies and a worst-first scorecard, so the next prose rule worth converting into a deterministic blocker is a measurement, not a guess.
acceptance: SessionStart parses CLAUDE.md into numbered rules, PostToolUse tallies, and SessionEnd renders the worst-first scorecard to the ledger dir

tasks.t: E9-S1-T1: lib/dead_rules.py plus its three hook integrations
tasks.risk: Relevance heuristics are approximate. The scorecard is advisory-only output and never blocks.

stories.title: SessionEnd cleanup and flush
stories.why: As an operator, I want session state cleaned and metrics flushed however the session ends, so state directories do not accrete.
acceptance: session_end.py flushes ledger buffers, renders pending scorecards, removes the session state dir, and stays fast (async where wired)

tasks.t: E9-S2-T1: session_end.py
tasks.risk: Long work here delays process exit. A hard time budget is asserted in the test.

stories.title: InstructionsLoaded audit log
stories.why: As the maintainer, I want a ground-truth log of which rule and skill files loaded and why, so checking whether an orphaned hook still loads is a one-line lookup.
acceptance: instructions_loaded.py appends file, load_reason, and ts to the ledger dir, runs async, and its output is ignored per docs

tasks.t: E9-S3-T1: instructions_loaded.py async logger
tasks.risk: None material, log-only.

stories.title: E9 wiring
stories.why: As the ADW maintainer, I want SessionEnd and InstructionsLoaded registered with async true.
acceptance: snippet entries with async true on both, routes added, merge tests updated. Covers the wiring half of the async-hooks idea

tasks.t: E9-W-T1: Wire SessionEnd plus InstructionsLoaded (async)
tasks.risk: None beyond shared-file sequencing.

epics.title: Rollout, live verification, docs
epics.outcome: The MVP slice is proven in a live session, gate defaults are a deliberate human decision on ledger evidence, and SKILL.md plus README document the new surface including parity gaps.

stories.title: Prove and decide
stories.why: As the owner, I want live proof that the events fire as planned and an evidence-based decision on which gates go default-on, so rollout is a decision, not a hope.
acceptance: E10-T0 first: a live session proves the Stop hook blocks and releases as documented, before any other new event goes live. The lead runs the install. This is the first pivot-or-persevere gate from validation.decision_rule

E10-T1 then verifies the full surface: SubagentStop scan, UserPromptSubmit inject, ConfigChange block, PreCompact snapshot plus compact re-inject, with a heartbeat requirement (at least one ledger row per wired event during the session) and the installed client version recorded next to the results
the gate promotion decision (observe to enforce) is recorded per family with the report's adjudicated false-signal rate and ledger numbers that justified it

SKILL.md and README are updated with new events, config keys, the parity matrix with its fallback column, and kill-switches, and block messages are reviewed for actionability (the block message is ADW's whole UI)

tasks.t: E10-T0: Live Stop smoke (the MVP experiment)
checks: python3 -c 'import glob,json,os,datetime; sid_path=os.path.expanduser("~/.agent-discipline/ledger/smoke-session.txt"); assert os.path.exists(sid_path), "smoke-session.txt missing"; sid=open(sid_path).read().strip(); assert sid, "smoke-session.txt empty"; rows=[json.loads(line) for path in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.agent-discipline/ledger/")+"*.jsonl") for line in open(path)]; stop_rows=[row for row in rows if row.get("family")=="stop" and row.get("session_id")==sid]; blocks=[row for row in stop_rows if row.get("outcome")=="block"]; releases=[row for row in stop_rows if row.get("outcome")=="release"]; assert blocks, "no stop block row in the recorded smoke session"; assert all(row.get("ts") for row in rows), "ledger row without ts, ledger corruption, E1-S1-T4 always writes ts"; utc=datetime.timezone.utc; norm=lambda value: (lambda parsed: parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=utc))(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(value)); pinned_all=[row for row in rows if row.get("session_id")==sid]; assert max(norm(row["ts"]) for row in pinned_all)>=max(norm(row["ts"]) for row in rows), "stale smoke-session.txt: another session holds newer ledger rows, re-pin the current smoke session"; first_block=min(norm(row["ts"]) for row in blocks); now=datetime.datetime.now(utc); assert abs(now-first_block)<=datetime.timedelta(hours=2), "stale evidence: the pinned smoke block is outside the two-hour live window"; assert any(norm(row["ts"])>=first_block for row in releases), "no release row at or after the block instant in the recorded smoke session"'
tasks.risk: This is where the event bet is settled, by design, at the smallest possible surface.

tasks.t: E10-T1: Full-event live verification
checks: python3 -c 'import glob,json,os,datetime; sid_path=os.path.expanduser("~/.agent-discipline/ledger/live-session.txt"); assert os.path.exists(sid_path), "live-session.txt missing"; sid=open(sid_path).read().strip(); assert sid, "live-session.txt empty"; rows=[json.loads(line) for path in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.agent-discipline/ledger/")+"*.jsonl") for line in open(path)]; pinned=[row for row in rows if row.get("session_id")==sid]; assert pinned, "no ledger rows in the recorded live session"; assert all(row.get("ts") for row in rows), "ledger row without ts, ledger corruption, E1-S1-T4 always writes ts"; utc=datetime.timezone.utc; norm=lambda value: (lambda parsed: parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=utc))(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(value)); newest=max(norm(row["ts"]) for row in pinned); assert newest>=max(norm(row["ts"]) for row in rows), "stale live-session.txt: another session holds newer ledger rows, re-pin the current verification session"; now=datetime.datetime.now(utc); assert abs(now-newest)<=datetime.timedelta(hours=2), "stale evidence: the pinned live session is outside the two-hour window"; seen={row.get("event") for row in pinned}; wired=set(json.load(open("hooks/claude-settings.snippet.json"))["hooks"]); missing=sorted(wired-seen); assert not missing, "no ledger row in the recorded live session for: "+", ".join(missing)'
tasks.risk: This is where residual event risk (risks[0]) surfaces for the non-Stop events.

tasks.t: E10-T2: Gate promotion decision (observe to enforce)
tasks.risk: Skipping this turns observe-mode staging into permanent limbo. It is scheduled, not optional.

tasks.t: E10-T3: SKILL.md plus README documentation pass
tasks.risk: Docs drift if gates change after E10-T2, so this task lands last.

epigraph.text: Your greatest difficulty is with yourself; for you are your own stumbling-block.
